_readme: SAIRNlaw deadline engine seed -- US Federal civil litigation (FRCP).
This is NOT run as a migration. It is loaded through api/legal-deadlines.js's
add_rule / add_holidays actions, which reject any rule lacking an authority
URL and stamp verified_by from the real session. That way every row was put
there by someone who read the rule, and the row records who and when --
the same discipline as sc_scrubrules and sc_credential_scope in SAIRNcode.
Every day count below was read from the primary source on 2026-08-21 and is
quoted in each rule's authority.quote field. None came from memory.
TWO RULES ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT, and the reason matters more than the
absence:
1. Fed. R. Civ. P. 12(a)(3) -- 'within 60 days after service on the officer
or employee or service on the United States attorney, WHICHEVER IS LATER'.
That is a two-trigger rule. The engine models one trigger event per rule,
so encoding it would silently compute from whichever trigger happened to
be supplied rather than the later of the two -- producing a date that is
too early roughly half the time. Too early is the dangerous direction.
It is omitted until the engine supports multi-trigger 'later of' rules.
2. The 90-day variant of 12(a)(1)(A)(ii) (waiver request sent to a defendant
outside any judicial district) is present but flagged: it shares a trigger
event with the 60-day variant and is distinguished only by a fact about
the defendant's location that the engine has no field for. Both are
included with DISTINCT trigger_event names so the user must state which
situation applies -- the engine will never guess between them, and
overlapping windows on one trigger would correctly raise AMBIGUOUS_RULE.
SERVICE EXTENSION, applied only where it genuinely applies: Rule 6(d) adds 3
days when a party 'may or must act within a specified time AFTER BEING
SERVED'. The waiver deadlines run from when the request was SENT, not from
service, so 6(d) is not attached to them. That is a deliberate omission, not
an oversight -- attaching it would extend a deadline that the rule does not
extend.

rules.label: Answer to a complaint after service of summons and complaint

authority.quote: within 21 days after being served with the summons and complaint

rules.label: Answer after a waiver request sent to a defendant within a judicial district

authority.quote: within 60 days after the request for a waiver was sent
authority.note: Runs from when the request was SENT, not from service, so Rule 6(d)'s 3-day service extension is not attached.

rules.label: Answer after a waiver request sent to a defendant outside any judicial district

authority.quote: or within 90 days after it was sent to the defendant outside any judicial district
authority.note: Distinct trigger_event from the 60-day variant on purpose: the engine must never guess which situation applies.

rules.label: Answer to a counterclaim or crossclaim

authority.quote: A party must serve an answer to a counterclaim or crossclaim within 21 days after being served with the pleading that states the counterclaim or crossclaim

rules.label: Answer by the United States, an agency, or an officer sued in an official capacity

authority.quote: must serve an answer to a complaint, counterclaim, or crossclaim within 60 days after service on the United States attorney

authority.note: Observed dates. Where a holiday falls on a Saturday the preceding Friday is observed; where it falls on a Sunday the following Monday is observed.
